title: Lab 8 — Quiz 2
subtitle: Simple Stains — differential stain IDs and smear technique

questions.prompt: Identify this differential stain: purple and pink cells in the same smear.
questions.explanation: Differential stains use two or more dyes to distinguish cell types. The Gram stain shows Gram+ (purple) and Gram− (pink).

why.A: Acid-fast stains show pink/red acid-fast cells and blue non-acid-fast cells.
why.C: A simple stain colors all cells the same.

questions.prompt: Identify this differential stain: green structures inside or beside pink cells.
questions.explanation: Endospore stain: endospores green, vegetative cells pink.

why.A: Gram stains are purple and pink only.
why.C: Acid-fast stains are pink/red and blue.

questions.prompt: Identify this differential stain: bright pink clumps mixed with blue cells.
questions.explanation: Acid-fast stain: acid-fast cells pink/red; non-acid-fast cells blue.

why.A: Gram stains are purple and pink.

questions.prompt: Which special stain is used to show this outer cell structure surrounding the cells?
questions.explanation: The capsule stain is listed among the differential stains (Gram, acid-fast, endospore, capsule, flagellar).

why.B: Flagellar stains show thin whip-like flagella.
why.C: Endospore stains show green spores inside cells.
why.D: Simple stains color whole cells one color.

questions.prompt: Which stain was used to show the thin, wavy appendages extending from these cells?

why.A: Capsule stains outline the capsule around cells.
why.B: Gram stains show cell wall type, not flagella.
why.C: Acid-fast stains detect mycolic acid walls.

questions.prompt: A simple stain differs from a differential stain because a simple stain:

options.text: Uses two or more dyes to distinguish cell types
Always requires heat as a mordant
Can only be used on yeast
Uses a single dye to color all cells the same (or the background)

questions.explanation: Simple: a single dye. Differential: two or more dyes to distinguish cell types or parts.

why.B: Heat mordants are for acid-fast and endospore stains.
why.C: Simple stains are used on bacteria and yeast.

questions.prompt: Which smear labels and organisms were used in Lab 8?

options.text: PB = Saccharomyces; PY = Bacillus; N = E. coli
PB = E. coli; PY = Candida; N = Cryptococcus
PB = Bacillus; PY = Candida; N = Bacillus
PB = Bacillus subtilis; PY and N = Saccharomyces cerevisiae

questions.explanation: PB: positive stain of Bacteria (Bacillus subtilis). PY: positive stain of Yeast and N: negative wet mount (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).

why.A: The bacterium is B. subtilis; the yeast is S. cerevisiae.
why.B: Lab 8 used B. subtilis and S. cerevisiae.
why.C: The yeast for both PY and N was S. cerevisiae.

questions.prompt: Smear preparation from a solid culture: which step comes first?

options.text: Place the bacteria directly on the dry slide
Place a loopful of sterile water on the slide
Add the stain to the slide

questions.explanation: Solid culture: loopful of sterile water on the slide → small loopful of bacteria stirred in → smear to nickel size → air dry → heat fix.

why.A: Bacteria from solid media are dispersed into a water droplet.
why.B: Heat fixing comes after the smear air dries.
why.D: Staining comes after smearing and heat fixing.

questions.prompt: Why is no water added when making the PY smear from yeast?

options.text: Water would kill the yeast cells
Yeast smears are not air dried
Yeast is heat fixed in water
Water is not needed for liquid cultures

questions.explanation: Water is needed to disperse organisms from solid media; it isn't needed for liquid cultures.

why.A: Water is used for solid cultures; liquid cultures already have liquid.
why.B: All smears are air dried before heat fixing.
why.C: Heat fixing is done on the dried slide.

questions.prompt: How big should the smear be?

options.text: About the size of a nickel
The entire length of the slide

questions.explanation: Smear the mixture over an area about the size of a nickel.

why.C: The organism is spread over about a nickel-sized area.
why.D: Thorough dispersion is crucial; thick smears are hard to read.

questions.prompt: This Staphylococcus smear was stained with a single purple dye. What kind of stain is it?
questions.explanation: Crystal violet used alone is a positive simple stain.

why.B: In a negative stain the cells stay clear against a dark background.
why.C: A Gram stain uses several reagents; this is one dye.
why.D: Acid-fast uses carbolfuchsin and methylene blue.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a basic dye used for positive simple staining?
questions.explanation: Basic dyes for simple stains include crystal violet, safranin and methylene blue.

why.A: India ink is anionic and used for negative staining.
why.D: Immersion oil improves resolution; it isn't a dye.

questions.prompt: When removing your loop from the stain droplet during the negative wet mount, what do you do before sterilizing it?

options.text: Rinse the loop with water over the staining tray
Sterilize it right away without rinsing it first
Wipe it clean on a page of bibulous paper
Dip it straight into the organism culture

questions.explanation: After the stain transfer, rinse the loop with water over the tray, then sterilize. After transferring the organism, sterilize WITHOUT rinsing.

why.B: After transferring the STAIN, rinse first; after the organism, don't rinse.
why.C: The protocol rinses the loop over the staining tray.
why.D: The loop is rinsed and sterilized before picking up the organism.

questions.prompt: A smear is stained without being heat fixed and then rinsed. What is the most likely result?

options.text: Much of the specimen washes off the slide
The stain turns into a negative stain

questions.explanation: Heat fixing secures/adheres the specimen to the slide; without it, rinsing removes cells.

why.B: Without fixing, cells aren't adhered and wash away.
why.C: Heat fixing doesn't affect spore formation.
why.D: Positive vs negative depends on the dye.

questions.prompt: Which statement about dyes is FALSE?

options.text: Basic dyes stick to cells and give them color
Acidic dyes often create a dark background
India ink is anionic but not acidic

questions.explanation: Basic dyes are CATIONIC (positively charged). Acidic dyes are anionic.

why.B: True — they are repelled by cells.
why.D: True — the nuance on the slide.
